newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch to pay $30 million to end probe.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch to pay $30 million to end probe.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co. agreed Thursday to pay $30 million to settle a 2-1/2-year investigation by the Orange County district attorney's office into the county's 1994 bankruptcy.
The agreement marked the end of the district attorney's probe of the powerful New York brokerage firm, and ensures that Merrill Lynch and its employees will not face criminal charges.
"There will be no criminal charges against Merrill Lynch or anyone else," District Attorney Michael Capizzi said.
Merrill Lynch said it agreed to the out-of-court settlement to avoid the "cost and distraction" of litigation.
"We continue to believe that we acted properly and professionally in all facets of our relationship with Orange County," the company said in a statement.

Orange County shocked Wall Street in December 1994 when it filed for bankruptcy after losing more than $1.6 billion on risky investments made by its once-respected treasurer, Robert Citron. The county emerged from bankruptcy one year ago.
An Orange County grand jury has been investigating various bond and investment firms, including Merrill Lynch, and other financial professionals in connection with the county's bankruptcy crisis.

The grand jury focused on Merrill Lynch's role as the underwriter of county debt offerings in 1994. The panel's deliberations have been kept secret, but rumours spread in recent weeks that indictments were likely.
The district attorney's office said the Merrill Lynch settlement capped a 2-1/2 year probe of public officials and Wall Street bond firms involved in the bankruptcy debacle.

Under the terms of the settlement, Merrill Lynch agreed to a $27 million payment to Orange County and to reimburse the $3 million cost of the district attorney's investigation. The firm also agreed to enhance the way it gathers, coordinates and discloses information about municipal bonds.
At a Santa Ana, Calif., news conference, Capizzi faced repeated questions from local reporters who wanted to know why Merrill Lynch would not face charges.

"When the civil settlement was arrived at, I felt it would provide everything we could hope to achieve," Capizzi said. "(The settlement) provides for what I think is a significant penalty as well as procedural changes within Merrill Lynch."
Orange County officials said the settlement would not have any effect on the county's $2-billion-plus civil lawsuit against Merrill Lynch.
"The civil litigation against Merrill Lynch will continue to be vigorously pursued. We continue to be confident that we will prevail," lead county attorney Bruce Bennett said.
Merrill Lynch said the county's lawsuit was without merit and vowed to continue to fight it in court.
Sources said the settlement would also have no effect on the Securities and Exchange Commission's probe of Merrill Lynch and other investment firms.
As previously reported, SEC staff has sent notices to at least two senior Merrill Lynch executives, informing them they may be charged in connection with the county bankruptcy.
